Sin Ming Avenue maisonette sets new executive flat record at $1.7 mil; Woodlands executive apartment sets $1.28 mil town record
article:
Two executive flats set new resale price highs in November, based on HDB resale data.

Executive maisonette at Sin Ming Avenue changes hands at $1.7 million, the highest price for an executive flat in Bishan

An executive maisonette at 442 Sin Ming Avenue was sold for $1.699 million ($1,018 psf) in November, the highest resale price recorded for an HDB executive flat. The 1,668 sq ft unit is on the 19th to 21st storeys and has about 62 years of lease remaining.

The sale surpasses the previous executive flat record of $1.65 million ($946 psf) , set in August by a 1,743 sq ft maisonette at 192 Bishan Street 13 .

Executive maisonettes such as the sunject flat are two-storey HDB flats, with living and bedroom areas split across two levels and linked by an internal staircase. They fall under HDB's executive flat category, which also includes single-level executive apartments. Floor areas typically exceed 1,500 sq ft. Their size and duplex layout may appeal to buyers looking for more space or a less common home format

HDB stopped building executive maisonettes in 1995, so they are only available on the resale market. As a result, every unit on the market is at least three decades old. This fixed supply may have helped support prices in recent years, even as remaining leases shorten.

That said, the maisonette is not the most expensive HDB flat in Bishan. The town record remains at $1.71 million ($1,325 psf), recorded in October for a five-room flat at 273A Bishan Street 24 (see Table 1).

On a psf basis, the gap between executive and five-room flats in Bishan is wide. The two executive flats in Table 1 sold for $946 and $1,018 psf. The three five-room flats sold for between $1,264 and $1,325 psf. The difference partly reflects lease. The executive flats have about 60 to 62 years remaining, against about 84 years for the Bishan Street 24 flats, with leases that began in 2011.

Nationally, the sale is the ninth-highest HDB resale price recorded, and the only executive flat in the top 10 (see Table 2). The highest resale price recorded is $1.818 million ($1,522 psf) . It was for a five-room flat at 96 Dawson Road in Queenstown, sold in October.

Table 2 does not include the $1.726 million sale of a five-room flat at Skyoasis @ Dawson in Queenstown, reported by EdgeProp Singapore in July 2024. The transaction does not appear in HDB's current resale dataset, although its price would rank it above the Sin Ming Avenue maisonette.

Location may also have contributed to the price. The flat is a 10-minute walk from Bright Hill MRT Station on the Thomson-East Coast Line (see Map 1). The station is slated to become an interchange with the Cross Island Line when the line's first phase opens in 2030, according to the Land Transport Authority. That phase will run from Bright Hill to Aviation Park, serving areas such as Ang Mo Kio, Serangoon North, Hougang, Pasir Ris, Tampines and Loyang. Residents near Bright Hill could gain a more direct rail link to the north-east and east.

The subject flat is also within 200m of Ai Tong School, the only primary school within a 1km radius. Peirce Secondary School is within 1km as well.

Beyond transport links and schools, the Sin Ming and Bright Hill area also has new private residential projects in the pipeline. The Thomson Reserve sold 1,143 of its 1,268 units (90.1%) across its VIP preview on October 30 and launch day on October 31, EdgeProp Singapore reported. The units sold at an average of $2,900 psf.

Meanwhile, a 99-year leasehold government land sales (GLS) site at Lorong Puntong and Sin Ming Avenue drew a top bid of $208.1 million ($1,612 psf ppr) from Malaysia's Eco World Development in September. The tender attracted seven bids, and the site could yield about 140 homes.

Executive apartment at Woodlands Street 81 sets a new record of $1.28 million for HDB flats in Woodlands

Up north, an executive apartment at 805 Woodlands Street 81 was sold for $1.28 million ($619 psf) in November, the highest resale price recorded for an HDB flat in Woodlands, based on HDB resale data. The 2,066 sq ft unit is on the 10th to 12th storeys and has about 66 years of lease remaining.

The sale surpasses the previous town record of $1.27 million ($666 psf), reported by EdgeProp Singapore in October 2025.  That transaction was for a 1,905 sq ft executive apartment at 850 Woodlands Street 82 (see Table 3).

Woodlands has recorded 37 million-dollar HDB resale transactions in 2026 as of November, up from 29 in the whole of 2025. These include a 1,582 sq ft executive apartment along the same street, which sold for $1.01 million in May . Its owners had bought the flat in 2019, EdgeProp Singapore reported in September.

Part of the flat's appeal may lie in its location. A short walk away, Woodlands MRT Station offers direct access to Orchard and the CBD on both the North-South and Thomson-East Coast lines (see Map 2). One stop up the latter is Woodlands North, the terminus for the five-minute Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link to Johor Bahru, slated to open in February 2027.

For families, Qihua Primary School is about 190m from the flat, while Woodlands, Evergreen, Woodgrove and Si Ling primary schools are all within 1km.

Daily needs are also close at hand. Causeway Point shopping mall, which is connected to Woodlands MRT Station, has a FairPrice supermarket alongside retail and dining options, while a Sheng Siong supermarket is across the road from Block 805.

More amenities could follow if a mixed-use white site at Woodlands Avenue 2 is sold. The URA Reserve List site, which has yet to be triggered for sale, could yield about 440 homes and 78,000 sqm (839,592 sq ft) of commercial space.

title: What's moving the market: Singapore's biggest property deals and hottest searches (Nov 27)
article:
Here is this week’s data-led look at Singapore’s property market, covering record transactions, rental benchmarks and the most searched homes on EdgeProp.

The following insights are compiled from EdgeProp Buddy , URA Realis and data.gov.sg, downloaded as of Nov 24.

Non-landed private homes — new launches, resales and rents

The most expensive condo unit sold during the fortnight to Nov 24 was a Park Nova apartment that changed hands for $14.8 million in a sub sale. Its price tag works out to $5,092 psf based on the four-bedroom unit’s area of 2,906 sq ft.

Located on Tomlinson Road in District 10, Park Nova is an ultra-luxury development with 54 units. Its highest-ever transacted price was $38.888 million, which also set the project’s psf-price record of $6,593 psf.

Lucerne Grand was the most transacted new launch condo during the past 14 days, with nine deals recorded. Elta followed with five, while Vela Bay had four transactions.

In the condo rental market, The Sail @ Marina Bay and Marina One Residences were the most popular in the Core Central Region (CCR), with 43 and 42 deals respectively.

The highest rent among CCR condos came from a four-bedroom apartment, measuring more than 3,000 sq ft, at The Marq On Paterson Hill. It is commanding $40,000 per month.

Located in District 9, The Marq On Paterson Hill has 66 units. It also accounted for two other condo units on the list, at $33,000 and $37,000.

title: NORDIC GROUP: Record Backlog, Record Profit Next? What Comes After?
article:
Nordic Group’s 3Q2026 results were already encouraging: revenue rose
13%
year on year while net profit climbed
31%
, taking 9M2026 profit to
S$15.8 million.

The subsequent management briefing provided a more interesting look at what could drive the engineering group in 2027 and beyond.

Executive Chairman Chang Yeh Hong.
File photo
The message was clear: demand is strong across marine, semiconductors and maintenance services, while Nordic’s record
S$286 million
order book provides more than a year of revenue visibility.

At the same time, in some businesses, the problem is no longer finding orders—it is having enough manpower, equipment and execution capacity to take them on.

Here are eight things that stood out from the briefing:

1
. Management is signalling strong FY26 profit

1
. Management is signalling strong FY26 profit

1
. Management is signalling strong FY26 profit

Management said FY26 revenue could exceed the previous annual high of about
S$162m.

More importantly, Executive Chairman Chang Yeh Hong again raised the prospect of a special dividend if
indeed 4Q lifts Nordic to a strong full-year profit.

indeed 4Q lifts Nordic to a strong full-year profit.

That would come on top of Nordic’s existing policy of distributing 40% of earnings.
For illustration, if Nordic's 4Q profit matches the 3Q figure of $5.8 million, the total FY26 net profit will reach a record
S$21.6 m
. Then, on 50 cent stock price:
• FY26 P/E: 9.2x
• Ordinary dividend: 2.17 cents (40% payout)
• Dividend yield: 4.34%, excluding any special dividend.

2. Cash generation is solid

Nordic’s net cash had already reached
S$20.1 million
at end-Sept, versus just S$4.1 million at end-2025, and should rise further in 4Q because there are fewer scheduled major cash outflows.

More strikingly, Mr Chang said that, absent major acquisitions or capital expenditure, Nordic could add around
S$30 million of cash a year
.

That means Nordic will have a capital-allocation problem of the good kind: how much to spend on capacity, acquisitions, dividends or share buybacks.

Management's preferred order appears to be:

Invest in capacity where returns are attractive.

Pursue acquisitions only if clearly accretive.

Otherwise return excess cash.

3. Marine segment looks particularly strong

3. Marine segment looks particularly strong

3. Marine segment looks particularly strong

3. Marine segment looks particularly strong

Mr Chang described the current shipbuilding cycle as a “golden era” potentially lasting another five to six years.
Nordic recently secured work on
51 vessels
from a single Chinese shipyard, illustrating the scale of series-vessel ordering now taking place.

Nordic supplies automation, flow-control and monitoring systems.

For FPSOs (Floating Production, Storage and Offloading vessels), the engineering work is considerably more complex.
When existing vessels are converted into floating oil production facilities, Nordic may need to redesign, upgrade and integrate existing control systems to meet new operational requirements.

Once installed, these systems also generate opportunities for higher-margin replacement parts, repairs and servicing throughout the vessel's operating life.

Mr Chang put it simply:

“What we want is really the FPSO conversions… because the margins are really good.”

He added that 2–3 FPSOs a year would be very good, and the current quoted pipeline includes around
11 FPSOs
.

That makes marine a strong earnings catalyst.

4. Semiconductor: huge opportunity

The semiconductor/project quotation pipeline has jumped to about
S$440m
, but only around
S$38m i
s currently classified as having mid-to-high probability of success.

An investor explicitly noticed that the high-conviction proportion has fallen from around 40% previously to
under 10% now
.

CEO of susbdiary Envipure, Jeanette Lee, explained that many of the new opportunities are very large, early-stage projects of
S$30m–70m each
.

She said semiconductor customers are in a “super cycle”, with Micron and others expanding simultaneously across Singapore, Malaysia, India, Thailand and Vietnam.

5. Capacity may become the constraint on earnings growth

Nordic effectively said it cannot accept every large semiconductor project because once it commits resources to one major project, it may have to turn down another.

Mr Chang said:

“It's not just getting the contracts but looking at the capability and the timing…”

That's both positive and negative.

Positive:
demand exceeds Nordic's existing capacity.

Negative:
FY27 growth may be constrained by manpower, equipment and execution bandwidth.

6. The defence-pipeline fall from S$170m to S$100m
is not worrying

6. The defence-pipeline fall from S$170m to S$100m
is not worrying

6. The defence-pipeline fall from S$170m to S$100m
is not worrying

6. The defence-pipeline fall from S$170m to S$100m
is not worrying

Mr Chang said the pipeline fell because:

Nordic secured some contracts;

two projects totalling roughly
S$30–40m
were abandoned by the end-users; and

Nordic itself dropped some fuel-tank work because margins were too low and capacity was tight.

The major defence projects also remain alive.
Mr Chang said one major project is now closer to tender award, while the Tengah air-base work is progressing first through A&A/integration work before the larger expansion project.

7. Thailand is real now—and moving fast

AviTools Thailand has now started mass production for the energy-storage programme.

Management expects only about US$0.2m in 4Q26, but around
US$5m revenue in FY27
from the current programme.

The customer is asking Nordic to ramp faster than expected, and management says current demand is already straining capacity.

So, the recurring theme is: Demand isn't the problem. Capacity is.

8.

One concentration risk: Micron

Management said
more than 50–60%
of its semiconductor opportunities are from Micron.

Nordic has worked with Micron for more than 40 years, so this is a very strong relationship—but it's still concentration.

The upside is that Nordic has followed Micron into
India
, winning its first project there, and hopes to build the same local base it previously created in Malaysia.

Takeaway

The outlook appears encouraging.

Mr Chang said Nordic’s current order book gives the group more than a year of visibility, and that further major awards during 2027 could stretch that visibility even further.

Importantly, maintenance remains the more predictable and traditionally better-margin side of the business.
The current order book is tilted toward projects because of recent large wins, but Nordic expects the mix to normalise as those projects complete.

Nordic is heading into 2027 with a record order book, rising cash, a strong marine cycle, semiconductor customers expanding rapidly, defence opportunities still in play and a new Thailand operation beginning to contribute.

title: India-US trade deal talks close to culmination, Goyal says
article:
(Nov 27): India’s trade deal negotiations with the US are “close to culmination,” Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said, days after Washington unveiled a tariff proposal that increases the pressure on New Delhi to reach an agreement.

“The process and pathway, which was always something which held back finalising the deal, is now taking some shape,” Goyal said in a virtual address in Mumbai on Friday.

His comments come after the Trump administration earlier this week proposed tariffs of up to 25% on goods imported from India, while saying the rate could be lowered to 17% if the two sides strike a trade deal. The lower rate would give India an advantage over Asian exporters including Vietnam, Malaysia and Bangladesh.

The proposal has intensified pressure on New Delhi to agree to a trade pact or face a higher levy, exposing exporters to more uncertainty. The proposed tariffs stem from a USTR Section 301 investigation into policies and practices it says contribute to structural excess manufacturing capacity and burden US commerce.

India has pushed back against such allegations. The government said in a statement that it had “engaged constructively” during the investigation, and that any trade-related concerns should be addressed through US-India talks towards a bilateral deal.

The two sides have been locked in negotiations over a trade deal since agreeing to a framework in February. The US trade probes, as well as a recently passed law on Russian oil sanctions, have complicated the negotiations.

See also: Shein’s slow India start lays bare limits of billionaire Ambani’s retail might — Bloomberg

Goyal also said the free trade pact with the EU would be “hopefully executed and signed later this year and come into effect by March or April next year.”

Bruised by US tariff policies, New Delhi has fast-tracked free trade negotiations with a host of economies, including Canada, Mexico, and Chile. It signed a slew of deals last year, and trade talks with the EU concluded earlier this year, with the agreement expected to be signed by year-end. A pact with Canada is likely to be concluded soon and announced during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to the nation next month.

title: Vietnam expects to sign US trade deal to limit tariff hit
article:
(Nov 27): Vietnam expects to sign a trade deal with the US that will result in a significantly lower final tariff rate as the two countries inch closer to a reciprocal trade agreement.

“Vietnam has recently made very strong commitments and has essentially concluded negotiations” on a trade agreement with the US, Prime Minister Le Minh Hung said in Hanoi Friday. “Currently, both sides are finalising technical details for the signing of the agreement and the applicable tax rates will be significantly lower than the maximum levels recently announced by the US.”

The signing and implementation of the agreement would provide “a stable and favourable environment for Vietnamese and US businesses and investors, as well as international investors,” Hung said. The Southeast Asian manufacturing hub has spent months negotiating with Washington, with transshipment and non-tariff barriers among the main sticking points.

The US has announced plans to impose new tariffs on 14 economies in Asia and Europe, with rates varying by country, although they could secure lower rates by cutting deals with Washington. The proposed US tariffs could rise as high as 35% for Vietnam versus 20% if a mutual deal is struck.

After the US announcement, Vietnam’s trade and industry ministry said it would fully participate in the next steps of the US investigation, including attending public hearings, presenting its views and responding to questions from the USTR.

Vietnamese foreign ministry officials also urged the US to make an “objective and balanced assessment” of efforts the country has made so far. Authorities are ready to share more information and clarify policies and regulations as the government continues direct consultations with US counterparts “in the spirit of goodwill,” Foreign Ministry spokesperson Pham Thu Hang said at a Thursday briefing. Vietnam and the US have completed discussions on most issues, with only a few matters remaining, Hang said.

See also: When export restraints are the lesser evil

Local companies have however been advised to develop risk-management strategies and contingency plans to cope with changes in the US tariff policy, Deputy Minister of Industry and Trade Luong Hoang Thai said.

Vietnam posted a US$191 billion trade surplus with the US in the first nine months of 2026, surpassing US$178 billion in all of 2025, US Census data show. At the same time, its deficit with China, which supplies most of its imports, ballooned.

title: Oil stockpiling to influence market in 2027, Energy Aspects says
article:
(Nov 27): Oil stockpiling will be important factor for the next couple of years, potentially tightening the market and aiding prices even with a projected global surplus, according to Energy Aspects Ltd.

Around 600 million barrels of inventories have been drawn down worldwide since the start of the Middle East war, so there’s a need to rebuild, said Amrita Sen, founder and director of the consultancy.

China will be the biggest stockpiler, and will add 160 million barrels of new storage capacity this year and next, she said in a Bloomberg TV interview. Beijing is already refilling inventories, plus the US is set to rebuild strategic stockpiles at a low level from the second quarter of 2027, Sen said.

Refiners in China, the world’s No. 1 oil importer, have boosted purchases this month, taking advantage of falling prices. Global benchmark Brent has plunged over the last few months as Persian Gulf exports recovered despite continued Iranian attacks on shipping. Energy Aspects is forecasting a global surplus of 1.2 million barrels a day next year.

Traders are “getting very complacent” and want to short oil, but they’re doing so at their own risk when stockpiles are low and the chance of production outages is high, Sen said, referring to recent incidents in Brazil and Norway. Refilling stockpiles would take time, she said.

“Inventory refilling is a multiyear story, with 2028 being the bigger one than 2027 especially as the conflict continues for the first half at least.”

See also: Oil set for weekly gain as Mideast attacks keep market on edge

Exporting Persian Gulf oil is likely to remain costly and inefficient, with higher freight costs effectively baked into the trade, Sen said. Logistics, rather than production capacity, may become the biggest constraint, she said in a separate interview, adding that Energy Aspects was seeing Iraq deferring loadings by more than a week, while ship-to-ship transfers and uncertainty around Hormuz transits create further friction.

“From a geopolitical point of view, we think this current status quo is the new reality,” Sen said in the TV interview.

title: Singapore talking to US to keep AI chip access, deputy PM says
article:
(Nov 27): Singapore is in talks with the US to retain access to advanced semiconductors, Deputy Prime Minister Gan Kim Yong said, after Washington tightened restrictions on chip exports to the Southeast Asian nation.

The country is reviewing its processes to ensure it is not a place for illicit chip trade, Gan said at an event in the city state on Friday, adding Singapore has a comprehensive system against those suspected of breaching laws.

Singapore has found itself at the centre of alleged smuggling of advanced Nvidia Corp processors to China. The Trump administration this month moved to apply more scrutiny to exports of processors to several countries, including Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Singapore, and limit any chip sales abroad when the data centre buying them plans to provide Chinese companies remote access to advanced AI chips and servers.

Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said last week he expects the US rules to have some impact on the transshipment volume of high-end chips that flow through the city state.

Nvidia’s manufacturing partners including Super Micro Computer Inc and Dell Technologies Inc have told buyers in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia that their orders won’t be delivered at the moment, the Financial Times reported on Thursday. The Singaporean government hasn’t confirmed whether shipments have been halted, according to Gan.

“We have not confirmed it, we are in the process of engaging our businesses,” Gan said. “We will continue to work with the US to see how we can help our businesses here continue to have secure access to high-end chips.”

See also: The next Claude may be in Singapore

Officials in Singapore have repeatedly said that while the country won’t help the US enforce its trade restrictions, the Southeast Asian country works diligently to protect the integrity of its own laws. Local police charged a fifth person in a fraud case linked to the export of computer hardware suspected of containing Nvidia chips in mid-November, the latest sign of the tightening scrutiny.

title: Toyota car sales fall for ninth month as China slump worsens
article:
(Nov 27): Toyota Motor Corp’s sales fell for a ninth straight month after strong demand for hybrid vehicles was overshadowed by a worsening slump in China.

Global sales in October, including those of subsidiary Daihatsu Motor Co, fell 6.3% from a year earlier to 940,809 units, the company said in a statement Friday. Production declined 9.4% to 953,989 vehicles.

Soaring gas prices, falling demand for non-electric vehicles in China and supply snags in the Middle East have seen the Japanese carmaker make and sell fewer cars for most of the year.

Toyota and Lexus brand sales fell 25% in China, where legacy manufacturers are losing ground as Chinese companies led by BYD Co flood the market with software-heavy, battery-powered cars. More recently, contractions in the world’s biggest passenger vehicle market have been affecting both foreign and domestic carmakers.

Toyota’s monthly sales also fell 5.7% in Japan, and 12% in India. Deliveries grew 6.5% in the US, however, thanks to strong demand for gas-electric hybrids.

Toyota has said hybrid sales are on track to exceed five million units for the first time in 2026.

See also: HSBC reorganises India support roles, impacting hundreds of jobs — Bloomberg

Momentum in the US, among other factors, emboldened Toyota to raise its operating profit outlook to ¥3.9 trillion (US$24.5 billion) for the fiscal year ending March 2027. Still, large importers have suffered sizable losses due to higher raw material costs stemming from the conflict in the Middle East.

title: Oil set for weekly gain as Mideast attacks keep market on edge
article:
(Nov 27): Oil was on track for the first weekly gain this month as attacks on energy infrastructure and tankers in the Middle East raised concerns escalating hostilities could disrupt exports.

Brent traded near US$96 a barrel and was up 4.3% this week, while West Texas Intermediate was around US$86. Tehran-backed Houthi militants attacked Saudi Arabia’s Jazan refinery on the Red Sea, temporarily halting some operations, after targeting its Ras Tanura hub in the Persian Gulf earlier this week.

A drone attack on Kuwait on Thursday killed two Italian civilians and injured two others, with the Gulf nation blaming Iran. The Islamic Republic denied it was responsible, according to Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi.

Risks to shipping also remain elevated. A tanker was struck in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, according to UK Maritime Trade Operations, following unconfirmed Iranian claims of other vessels hitting mines. Still, traffic has risen through the waterway this month, helping to keep prices in check.

Markets are starting to price in the “inherent instability of the status quo”, said Saul Kavonic, an energy analyst at MST Marquee. “If the market starts to see volumes dropping materially in the face of increased attacks, then oil prices may head back to about US$100” a barrel, he added.

Global benchmark Brent is down almost a fifth this month after a revival in Middle East exports, which the International Energy Agency says will drive the market into a surplus this quarter. US President Donald Trump has also held off on renewed attacks on Iran following the US midterm elections.

See also: Opec+ considering sticking with current quotas, delegates say

Oil-product markets are seeing some relief, with diesel futures in Europe and pump prices in the US declining. The industrial fuel had rallied even harder than crude because of disruptions stemming from the US-Iran war and escalating Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries.

Traders will be closely watching an Opec+ meeting on Sunday as the group plots a course for 2027 supply. The alliance is considering keeping its current output quotas through January, as members remain at odds over how much they can sustainably pump.

See also: Oil holds two-day gain as Mideast tensions fuel market jitters

title: China hedge fund star builds operating system kernel for AI
article:
(Nov 27): An artificial intelligence startup founded by one of China’s most successful hedge fund managers is preparing to release its first product — the core of an operating system designed for AI agents rather than humans.

Feng Ji, the founder of the US$4 billion hedge fund Baiont Quant, is betting the program will help redefine the relationship between AI programs and the hardware needed to run them. After years of large language models making startling progress despite largely running on legacy operating systems like Windows or Linux, the idea is to write operating systems explicitly tailored for AI.

The plan gives a glimpse into how China’s AI hopefuls are approaching a technology that is shaking up the global economy. While US firms like Anthropic and OpenAI are competing over who can build the most powerful frontier models, the focus in China has tended to be narrower — and often more practical.

The country has become a hotbed for AI agents, which can help users with a range of tasks like responding to emails, making reservations at restaurants or checking in to flights. The popularity of AI agents among Chinese citizens fuelled a frenzy around the popular OpenClaw program earlier this year, leading to engineers being inundated with requests by less tech-savvy citizens who wanted help installing the agent.

Feng’s startup, Cosmic Dawn, plans to release the so-called kernel by the end of this year. The term refers to a program that essentially provides the plumbing for an operating system, providing guardrails for things like file access and memory management.

He will then roll out the new system across his quant firm, with the aim of further automating research. “Everybody at Baiont will be using it because it’s efficient, especially when deploying a large number of agents during research,” he said.

See also: Huawei teases next-gen AI memory chip to take on Samsung, Hynix

The startup completed a seed round of fundraising at a post-money valuation of roughly two billion yuan (US$300 million), mostly from Chinese investors, before the team was formed, Feng said, declining to provide more details. He plans to start a second round around the first quarter of 2027.

​Kernel-level safeguards could help prevent AI agents from exceeding their authority, while systems capable of coordinating large numbers of agents could find promising applications in servers and specialised devices, said Tian Feng, dean of Beijing-based Thinking, Fast and Slow Institute.

“Cosmic Dawn has correctly identified the problem: AI agents need their own identities, permissions, budgets and memory,” said Tian, who was also the founding dean of Alibaba Cloud’s research institute. But he added that since Cosmic Dawn hasn’t publicly released code or performance tests, it’s too early to tell whether the technology is really unique.

See also: Viettel, Singtel building subsea cable for data-hungry Vietnam

Other Chinese firms are pursuing similar ambitions, albeit with slightly different technical approaches. In July, AI startup StepFun unveiled Step AOS, which it called the world’s first agent-native operating system. Rather than developing an entirely new kernel, StepFun adapted the Android kernel and built its agent layer on top of it.

Feng, who holds a PhD in machine learning from Nanjing University, has made AI central to his hedge fund. It performs everything from data mining to strategy development and execution, he said.

Baiont’s roughly 70 staff are mostly science and engineering graduates, and no-one in the around 50-member investment and research team is from a finance background, according to Feng. Baiont’s CSI 1000 Index enhanced fund has generated a cumulative return of more than 100% as of Nov 6 since its inception in January 2023, Feng said, eclipsing the performance of the index.

title: Gold rises as rebound in tech stocks offsets rate-hike concerns
article:
(Nov 27): Gold rose as a tentative recovery in technology stocks and a weaker US dollar offset the prospect of interest-rate hikes by the Federal Reserve (Fed).

Bullion climbed as much as 1.7% to near US$3,627 an ounce, on track for a weekly gain after rebounding from a 15-month low two days ago. Asian stocks advanced for a second day, extending a rally following weeks of volatility in the artificial intelligence trade, while a gauge of the dollar fell 0.1%, making bullion priced in the US currency cheaper for most buyers.

Sentiment remains fragile, however, at the end of a choppy week of trading. The yellow metal has remained below US$4,000 an ounce since Nov 11 as traders gauged the Fed’s path for combating sticky inflation. It’s still on track for a third monthly loss of more than 6%, extending a fall from a record high in January that gained pace after the US-Iran war sent energy costs soaring.

The Fed’s preferred measure of underlying inflation for October, released Wednesday, reinforced expectations that the central bank will tighten policy when it meets in December. Higher borrowing costs are typically negative for gold, which doesn’t pay interest. The market is also weighing the likelihood of further rate hikes early next year if price pressures continue.

“Gold faces a critical support zone between US$3,450 and US$3,500, the area from which prices broke out in August 2025 before staging their historic rally to record highs,” said Hebe Chen, senior market analyst at Vantage Global Prime. “This is now the line in the sand for gold — holding above this zone could provide a foundation for stabilisation, while a decisive break below would raise the risk of a deeper correction.”

Spot gold climbed 1.4% to US$3,616.36 an ounce at 10.24am in Singapore. Silver surged 3.6% to US$43.04 an ounce. Platinum and palladium also advanced.

title: IMF sees emerging risks in Australia’s US$3.1 tril of pensions
article:
(Nov 27): The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has flagged a series of emerging risks in Australia’s fast-growing pension system, including the challenge of keeping more assets liquid as a wave of workers enters retirement.

While the IMF said the A$4.7 trillion (US$3.1 trillion) system is largely resilient to liquidity shocks, it identified a range of challenges in a report Friday. They include rising cyber risks, greater competition that makes it easier for members to switch funds, and the need to hold more liquid assets as a growing number of retirees draw down their savings.

The increasing share of assets held offshore is also likely to drive growth in currency hedging, with potential implications for banks, the IMF said. Around half of the sector’s assets are invested overseas.

“These structural shifts will require continuous adaptation of the regulatory framework and place increasing demands on supervisory resources,” the IMF said. “The superannuation sector is maturing and new developments, such as AI, create new opportunities but may also change how risks may materialise in the future.”

Australia’s pension system regularly ranks among the world’s top retirement systems and is set to be larger than Canada’s by the early 2030s. Still, the challenge of an estimated 2.5 million people retiring in the next decade is reshaping the system.

The IMF’s concerns echo comments from the Reserve Bank of Australia, which last month warned the cushion of inflows for the sector and the broader financial system may become less dependable over time as more funds move into net cash-outflow positions as more people retire.

See also: US targets major trading partners with new tariffs citing overcapacity

The report makes 13 recommendations, including more liquidity stress testing and deeper data collection.

title: JPMorgan, BlackRock bid for slice of $701 bil Singapore fund
article:
(Nov 27): JPMorgan Asset Management, BlackRock Inc and Endowus Singapore Pte Ltd are the frontrunners to manage a slice of Singapore’s $701 billion public pension fund.

The three firms submitted proposals to run a new investment programme that offers an alternative for members of the Central Provident Fund who want to earn more than the government-guaranteed return, according to people familiar with the matter. The winners will be announced in the first half of 2027. Discussions are preliminary and no final decisions have been made, said the people, who asked not to be identified discussing private matters.

JPMorgan would partner with Singapore’s largest bank, DBS Group Holdings Ltd, in an extension of a retirement portfolio programme that was piloted in 2024. Endowus, an investment platform, is in talks to work with Capital Group on the CPF programme, said the people.

A spokesperson for the CPF Board said the evaluation process is ongoing, and it can’t comment on individual applications. JPMorgan and Capital Group declined to comment. Endowus said it has been a digital adviser for investing CPF savings since 2019. BlackRock and DBS didn’t respond to requests for comment.

The investment plan was unveiled by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in this year’s budget speech as a way to deal with the country’s ageing population, and will be launched in 2028.

The new programme will allow members to opt in to portfolio strategies that automatically adjust according to their age. As investors get older, the equity allocation will shift to lower-risk assets such as bonds, before being liquidated in phases by a set target date.

See also: MindChamps founder seeks $86 mil for first preschool fund

Currently, members have the option of manually picking investments, including bonds, stocks and unit trusts, from a list of more than 30 asset managers. As of September, just $22 billion — or 3% — of net assets were invested in this optional plan, according to the CPF website.

The bulk of CPF savings are invested by the pension board in Special Singapore Government Securities. Proceeds from these securities are pooled with other government funds, including from budget surpluses and land sales, and managed by sovereign wealth fund GIC Pte for long-term returns. Members under 55 earn risk-free interest of up to 5% a year.

Founded in 1955, the CPF is Singapore’s mandatory pension fund for citizens and permanent residents to support retirement, housing and health-care needs. There are more than two million active members, and over $14 billion in CPF contributions were received in the third quarter.

title: GIC seeks to offload embattled renewable energy firm’s debt — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 27): Sovereign wealth fund GIC is having preliminary discussions to sell €300 million (US$329 million or $425 million) of debt from Spanish renewable energy company Forestalia Renovables SL, according to people familiar with the matter.

Distressed debt firm IG4 Capital Group is weighing a purchase of the debt at a discount but no decision has been made yet, said the people, who asked not to be named discussing private conversations. Houlihan Lokey Inc is advising GIC on the sale, some of the people said.

In 2021, GIC agreed to a seven-year loan to Forestalia’s holding company. The money was set to help the energy firm repay existing debt, inject capital into its businesses and help finance its project pipeline growth.

But earlier this year, Forestalia came under criminal investigation in Spain over environmental permits and public loans. Founder Fernando Samper stepped down from the company in April, handing the reins to his son, Ricardo Samper.

GIC is looking to offload its stake amid concerns that the allegations against the energy firm could severely impact the business, the people said.

IG4, founded about a decade ago by a team of four Brazilian investors, has built a reputation of jumping into complicated turnaround situations, including the restructuring of petrochemical company Braskem SA. That firm, one of the biggest victims of Brazil’s brutal credit cycle, has been seeking to restructure US$11 billion ($14 billion) of debt.

See also: UK energy bills rise 26% as war fuels cost-of-living squeeze

title: Bankers pay up for Hong Kong apartments as rents hit new highs
article:
(Nov 27): Hong Kong’s booming rental real estate market is spurring gains in previously underappreciated neighbourhoods, as bankers pay up for apartments in one of the world’s most expensive places to live.

Ho Man Tin is luring finance professionals to the upscale neighbourhood that’s near top schools and is close by to an area soon to house new office space for JPMorgan Chase & Co. Rents in the area are up more than 15%, almost double the pace of Hong Kong’s wider property market. Those in the increasingly popular Tseung Kwan O, far from the Central business district but connected by the underground rail network, are up 10%.

The old favourites are getting plenty of demand, too: Rents in Mid Levels, popular among European bankers attracted by its offering of restaurants and fancy delis, are up by double digits. Those in the Peak, home to many of the city’s richest people, have jumped more than 9%.

Across the city, a sentiment shift that has fuelled a surge in initial public offerings and an office leasing rush among financial institutions is pushing rents ever higher. Hong Kong’s rental price index of private homes jumped 6.3% in the first 10 months of this year, and average rental levels have repeatedly pushed to new record highs.

The frenzy is putting the pressure on potential renters, who are facing brief property listings and the risk of a form of a gazumping — a term from the market for home sales where buyers agree a deal and then find themselves pushed aside as a higher bid comes in at the last minute.

“The market hasn’t been this busy since at least 2018,” said Victoria Allan, founder and CEO of Habitat Property Ltd, which specialises in luxury properties. “We see shortages across all budget ranges, and some single-landlord buildings in Hong Kong Island south and Central have seen waiting lists.”

See also: New World just 1% of Henry Cheng’s US$27 bil fortune

Gary Lee, an investment banker who leases a 600-square-feet apartment near his office in Central, said he didn’t hesitate when his landlord recently asked for a 10% increase in rent.

“I don’t think I could find a similar available flat easily these days,” said the 35-year-old. Apartments “offering such convenience on transportation and shopping choices in nearby areas are limited”.

See also: New World considering rights issue as Bain walks away — Bloomberg

Competition for rentals is being driven both by tight supply and a surge in demand. Expats are returning, white-collar workers and students are arriving from mainland China, and more confident local professionals are choosing to rent. Hordes of foreigners are streaming back to grab white-collar jobs, responding to planned tax breaks for private equity and hedge funds.

There’s also the impulse of government-led programmes designed to lure skilled professionals. More than 410,000 such approvals were granted over the last three years, with almost three-quarters arriving from mainland China, government data in March showed.

Banking and fund management pros as well as high-net-worth individuals moving to the city through talent schemes are a major driver of rental growth, especially at the high-end, according to a residential leasing report by Savills plc. With demand running ahead of available supply, landlords have gained greater pricing power and are increasingly preferring tenants from the financial services sector, the report shows. The international property consultancy expects luxury residential rents will increase as much as 5% in the final quarter of this year.

It’s now a more ferocious environment where quick decisions can make or break a deal.

“For years, a landlord’s asking price was always subject to negotiation, but now it’s a different story,” said property agent Sonam Thadani, who counts finance workers as one of her major client bases. “We are coming to see tenants offering more than the asking price and willing to put down a deposit on the same day to secure a lease, especially where location and recent refurbishments offer limited competing options.”

Median asking prices for rents across Hong Kong rose about 7.9% in the first 10 months of 2026, with no neighbourhood recording a decline over that period, according to property platform Spacious.hk. The average time for each listing is also getting shorter, the data show. A typical two-bedroom flat around the prime Central area is fetching at least HK$25,000 (US$3,190 or $4,116) per month, not too far away from the average level in New York or Boston.

Among popular areas, Ho Man Tin, an enclave in the centre of the Kowloon peninsula, emerged as the new winner on rental growth. It offers greater proximity to bankers working in West Kowloon and wealthy mainland Chinese families with children at international schools nearby, according to James Fisher, chief operating officer of Spacious. JPMorgan is expected to move one of its offices into the West Kowloon area in 2028.

Jennifer Zuo, a wealth management professional who moved to Hong Kong from Shanghai earlier this year, eventually settled on a fully furnished serviced apartment on the east side of Hong Kong island.

Zuo, who stumps up around HK$40,000 a month for the apartment, has already started thinking about her next move. Her rent will be up for negotiation next year — and she’s anticipating an increase.

title: HSBC reorganises India support roles, impacting hundreds of jobs — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 27): HSBC Holdings Plc is consolidating some support functions in India as the Asia-focused lender steps up efforts to rein in costs and accelerate the adoption of artificial intelligence.

The bank recently told employees in India that it was centralising finance functions across cities including Chennai, Gurugram and Bangalore and will no longer be housing those roles in other hubs, including Hyderabad and Pune, according to people with knowledge of the matter, who requested not to be named because the information is private.

The changes are confined to finance roles within HSBC’s so-called global capability centres in India, and employees expect the move to affect several hundred roles, according to the people. HSBC staff will be given the option and support to relocate, but the bank won’t provide further cash incentives for them to move, the people added.

HSBC has been weighing deep job cuts over the coming years as chief executive officer Georges Elhedery deploys AI to shrink its middle and back offices. Non-client facing roles in global service centres are among those expected to be most impacted, people familiar have said previously. The changes could ultimately impact around 20,000 roles — or about 10% of its total workforce.

“As we simplify the bank, our focus remains on ensuring we have the right roles in the right locations to support the best customer outcomes,” an HSBC spokesperson said in a statement, referring to the roles in India. “We are taking the best of our people experience and combining this with emerging technologies to deliver outcomes that are better, faster, and safer for our clients.”

India has emerged as a key market for HSBC, alongside other major banks. HSBC describes itself as the largest foreign lender in the country and generated US$1.9 billion of pretax profit in the region in 2025. It had about 47,000 employees in India at the end of last year. About 42,500 employees work in the global capability centres in India, including on technology, according to estimates from a person familiar with the matter.

See also: Vietnam weighs delaying nuclear power plants beyond 2035 target

Other banks have also been reshaping their Indian hubs, which have grown so large that Goldman Sachs Group Inc and JPMorgan now employ more people in India than anywhere else outside the US. They are using AI to automate work such as checking loan documents, reconciling accounts and writing basic code, the same tasks that once gave fresh graduates their first jobs at those centers.

Lenders globally are expecting AI to lead to fewer roles in the future. Standard Chartered Plc plans to cut close to 8,000 support roles over four years, while JPMorgan Chase & Co CEO Jamie Dimon has said the technology will eliminate jobs broadly across industries. Banks are trimming junior analyst classes by as much as two-thirds, Debasish Patnaik, a senior partner at McKinsey & Co, said in June.

At HSBC, Elhedery has accelerated an overhaul of Europe’s largest bank through asset sales and operational simplification.

See also: Tata Trusts back lawsuit against Tata Sons chair’s reappointment — Bloomberg

In August, the lender said it expects its global restructuring effort to yield US$2 billion in cost savings, up from an earlier target of US$1.5 billion. The banker has made streamlining HSBC a central principle, saying earlier this year that he had been “ruthless about killing complexity” at the lender.

title: Asian stocks rise for second day, Treasuries slip
article:
(Nov 27): Asian stocks rose for a second day, extending a tentative recovery after weeks of volatility in the artificial intelligence (AI) trade. Treasuries declined as cash trading resumed following the Thanksgiving holiday.

MSCI Inc’s Asia Pacific equities gauge climbed 0.6%, with 10 of its 11 subsectors advancing. Three shares rose for every one that declined in the gauge. The Nikkei 225 in Japan gained 0.7% and the Kospi Index in South Korea advanced 1.5%.

Shares in Japan Tobacco climbed over 3% in Tokyo as the cigarette maker explored a potential takeover of Imperial Brands plc with Altria Group Inc.

Contracts for the S&P 500 Index and the Nasdaq 100 held Thursday’s gains and climbed around 1% ahead of a shortened Wall Street session Friday. While the US markets were closed Thursday, stocks in Asia and Europe staged a recovery from the volatility in the AI trade. The upbeat tone lifted copper almost 2% from an 11-month low in London.

Meanwhile, oil headed for the first weekly gain this month as attacks on energy infrastructure and tankers in the Middle East raised concerns about escalating hostilities. Brent crude opened little changed after rising more than 2% to above US$96 a barrel on Thursday. Elsewhere, Treasuries fell as cash trading resumed, with the yield on the benchmark 10-year rising four basis points to 4.90%.

Investors will be watching whether Thursday’s tech rally across Asia and Europe has staying power after days of volatility driven by doubts over the AI trade. Sentiment remains fragile, with traders seeing few catalysts to sustain the rebound as they look to next month’s Federal Reserve meeting for signals on the path of borrowing costs.

See also: Asian stocks rise as tech gains in Taiwan, South Korea

“The market seems to be stabilising,” said Gerald Gan, chief investment officer at Reed Capital Partners. “Although it could be a dead cat bounce, our base case still suggests that we will have a final meltup till the end of the year.”

In other corners of the market, bitcoin traded around US$60,600. Gold held its losses from the previous session, when it fell 0.6% to about US$3,565 an ounce — trading near levels last seen about 15 months back.

In New Zealand, the kiwi fluctuated after official election results confirmed a potentially hung parliament.

Meanwhile, futures for diesel in Europe have sunk almost 30% from a peak early in the US-Iran war, with a marked drop this month.

The fuel that powers the global economy is finally catching a break after months of war that drove prices close to a record, offering consumers, businesses and central bankers at least a temporary respite.

In other developments, Spain’s Pablo Hernandez de Cos is set to become European Central Bank president when Christine Lagarde leaves in February.

In Brazil, assets soared in anticipation Bradesco Chairman Luiz Carlos Trabuco Cappi would be announced as finance minister, giving investors some hope over the direction of fiscal policy.

Traders remain cautious on the AI trade as they wait for clues on the path for interest rates. Swap traders are fully pricing in a 25 basis point hike by the Fed in its December meeting.

Next week, Nvidia Corp’s newly reinstated chief executive officer Jensen Huang is scheduled to appear behind closed doors for a transcribed interview before three House committees probing the company’s China chip business. Huang is also scheduled to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on US chip-export controls.

Markets have whipsawed since the US midterm elections, with a leadership crisis at Nvidia adding to the turbulence and a selloff pushing major equity gauges into corrections.

“For the moment, I think the AI/Semiconductor trade is on hold,” said Neil Newman, head of strategy at Astris Advisory Japan. “We are not out of the woods yet by any measure.”

title: Marco Polo Marine earnings drop 44% y-o-y to $32.9 mil due to one-offs; defers PKR Offshore listing submission
article:
Mainly due to one-offs and exceptional items, Mainboard-listed Marco Polo Marine (MPM) has reported a 44% y-o-y decline in patmi to $32.9 million for FY2026 ended Sept 30. Revenue rose 24% y-o-y to $152 million.

On a diluted basis, EPS dropped around 45% to 0.85 cents. A final dividend of 0.2 cents has been declared, up from the previous year’s 0.15 cents.

The overall decline in earnings was mainly due to one-off items in FY2025 — the $22.4 million reversal of impairment loss on property, plant and equipment (which dropped to $2.0 million in FY2026), and the one-off gain of $5.9 million from disposal of a joint venture. Adjusted for these and other one-offs/exceptional items, underlying earnings increased 24% to $31.1 million.

Segmentally, ship chartering revenue increased 16% y-o-y to $93.1 million, mainly due to an expanded offshore vessel fleet. Shipyard revenue rose 38% y-o-y to $58.9 million, driven mainly by a higher volume of ship repair projects with the addition of a fourth dry dock in August 2025.

The company generated $79.5 million in net cash from operations, up from $40.8 million of the previous corresponding period. The higher cash generation is partially due to $25.5 million of contract liabilities (payment collected ahead of goods/services provision).

Cash and equivalents stood at nearly $139 million as at Sept 30, 2026, compared to $52.2 million of the previous corresponding period. Total borrowings was nearly $83.6 million, up from the previous $42.3 million.

See also: Nam Lee Pressed Metal Industries earnings rise 28.8% y-o-y to $32 mil

The company also announced that subsidiary PKR Offshore will defer the submission of its listing application in Taiwan from the third quarter of 2026 to the third quarter of 2027, with the aim of launching when conditions better reflect the value of its offshore wind business.

Nonetheless, MPM continues to see “meaningful” long-term growth opportunities for offshore wind in North Asia, underpinned by the energy transition and energy security priorities. However, the pace of development will depend on the timing of auctions and project awards, and the effect of higher financing costs on project economics, notes the company.

MPM expects charter rates and utilisation in its Southeast Asian markets to” remain firm” over the next 12 months, mainly due to constrained offshore support vessel supply in Southeast Asia arising from a decade of limited newbuild ordering and an ageing regional fleet.

See also: Coliwoo posts 7.6% higher Patmi for FY2026, declares special dividend

MPM CEO Sean Lee says that FY2026 was a year of “strong” operational delivery, adding that the proposed listing of MPM’s shipyard business positions the company for further growth and “long-term value creation” for its shareholders.

For context, MPM announced in September of a conditional sale and purchase agreement with Catalist-listed Fuji Offset Plates Manufacturing (FOPM), under which FOPM will acquire the entire issued share capital of Marco Polo Shipyard Pte Ltd and MP Marine Pte Ltd for up to $139.0 million. On completion, FOPM will be renamed MPSE Ltd. and become a separately listed platform for the MPM’s shipyard business, with MPM as its controlling shareholder.

Shares in MPM closed flat at 9.3 cents on Nov 26.
